claims.explanation: Atorvastatin's selective antiproliferative effect is most plausibly driven by inhibition of HMGCR-mediated mevalonate pathway flux, which is required for geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate-dependent prenylation of small GTPases (RAS, RHO, RAC) that sustain proliferation and survival. Lines with constitutive activation of RAS/MAPK or PI3K-AKT signaling, or with loss of negative regulators such as PTEN or NF1, are expected to be more dependent on this prenylation flux and therefore more sensitive, while intact feedback or low pathway activity confers protection.

features.basis: Loss of PTEN hyperactivates PI3K-AKT, increasing dependence on mevalonate-derived prenylation; PTEN-mutant lines (FTC133, UACC62, HEC265, KALS1) are enriched among sensitive lines
NF1 loss activates RAS-MAPK, which requires prenylated RAS; NF1-mutant lines (FTC133, LOXIMVI, S117, KALS1) are enriched among sensitive lines
BRAF V600 mutations drive MAPK signaling dependent on prenylated RAS/RHO GTPases; BRAF-mutant melanomas (K029AX, LOXIMVI, UACC62, IPC298, HEC265) are enriched among sensitive lines
Mutant NRAS requires farnesylation/geranylgeranylation for membrane localization and signaling; NRAS-mutant lines (KU1919, IPC298) appear among sensitive lines
KRAS-driven tumors depend on prenylation for oncogenic signaling; KRAS-mutant lines (SNU410, CL11) are among sensitive lines, though some KRAS lines are resistant, suggesting context dependence
Higher HMGCR expression implies greater mevalonate pathway flux and dependence on the drug's target, predicting stronger growth inhibition
TP53-mutant lines are common in both sensitive and resistant groups, but intact p53-mediated stress responses may enhance statin-induced apoptosis in some contexts; the pattern is weak and likely not
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (NCIH1650, NCIH1648, HCC4006) are among the least affected, suggesting EGFR-driven survival signaling may bypass mevalonate dependence
STK11/LKB1 loss alters metabolic stress responses and may increase dependence on mevalonate pathway intermediates; STK11-mutant lines (SNU840, KALS1) appear among sensitive lines
KEAP1/NRF2 pathway mutations may alter redox and metabolic dependencies; HEC265 (KEAP1/NFE2L2 mutant) is sensitive, but evidence is limited to few lines
ARID1A loss may impair chromatin remodeling and increase sensitivity to metabolic stress; ARID1A-mutant lines (LOXIMVI, KU1919, HEC265) are enriched among sensitive lines
SF3B1 mutations alter splicing and may create dependencies on mevalonate pathway flux; SF3B1-mutant lines (UO31, HCC95) appear among sensitive lines, but evidence is weak
